key_insight: ST2M uses crystal symmetry to guide generation, improving the joint yield of stable, unique, and novel structures under prescribed crystallographic constraints.
engineering_relevance: Symmetry-constrained generation could focus computational screening on viable crystal candidates and accelerate materials discovery.
method: Represent crystals as sequences of independent occupied Wyckoff orbits.
Condition discrete–continuous diffusion on Wyckoff patterns and apply degree-of-freedom masks.
Use a twin-branch Transformer to jointly denoise discrete and continuous variables.
evidence_signal: ST2M reports 96.37% structural validity and a 23.86% stable–unique–novel yield for known patterns, a 68.15% relative gain over the best baseline; first-principles calculations identify 21 previously unreported stable structures among selected low-predicted-energy candidates.
watch_item: First-principles validation covers selected candidates, and the abstract does not quantify performance on unknown Wyckoff patterns.
paper_title: Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation
